Which iPad calendar apps offer useful month and week views with weather for planning? Compare suitable options, distinguish a full calendar view from a widget and cite current official product sources.

For an iPad calendar that combines proper month and week planning views with weather forecasts, my strongest recommendations are Calendars by Readdle, Fantastical, Calendar 366, and Timepage.

The important distinction is whether weather appears inside the actual calendar app, alongside your appointments, rather than only in a Home Screen widget.

These are actual calendar/planning apps, not simply weather widgets. The strength of their weather integration differs.

Closer look at the strongest choices

1. Calendars by Readdle — best overall

Its official documentation explicitly confirms that weather can be enabled in Month, Week, Day and List views on iPad. This is the clearest match for seeing appointments and weather together.

Weather is documented under Calendars Premium. 
Calendars Knowledge Base
+1

Official weather documentation

2. Fantastical — best advanced calendar

Full-screen Month and Week views, drag-and-drop rescheduling, customizable layouts, and tasks. Flexibits advertises a 10-day AccuWeather forecast integrated into all calendar views, with event-location weather details.

A 10-day forecast does not mean weather predictions for an entire future month. Check Premium entitlements. 
Calendar Views
+1

Official features

3. Calendar 366 — best layout customization

Offers continuous or separated month layouts, week views configurable from 3 to 14 days, and Apple Weather forecasts in calendar views. Weather can follow your device location or a fixed location.

Good for detailed weekly planning, although the documentation does not establish that weather appears in every month-grid cell. 
Documentation
+1

Official documentation

4. Timepage — best visual experience

Weather is incorporated into the weekly timeline and day views, including richer forecast information. A month view is available, but its strongest weather-planning experience is the timeline rather than a weather-filled month grid.

Its separate Month and Week widgets should not be confused with the in-app views.

Other options worth considering

Cloud Calendars: Sync & Widget supports full Day, Week, Month, Year and List views, alongside hourly and daily forecasts and separate weather/calendar widgets. Its developer's App Store description confirms both features, but is less precise about weather placement in each grid. 
App Store

Weekwise is useful for planning the next eight days, with weather beside each day and hourly details on demand. It is not a substitute for a conventional full-month calendar.

For example, Fantastical has both a full-screen month view and a separate month widget. Timepage also has separate Month and Week widgets. Their existence alone does not establish that weather is displayed in the full month calendar.

My recommendation

Start with Calendars by Readdle if weather visibly integrated into both month and week views is your top requirement.

Choose Fantastical if sophisticated event scheduling matters equally, especially with its advertised 10-day forecast.

Try Calendar 366 if you want more control over how many days and weeks appear on your iPad.

One limitation applies to all of them: a full month calendar is not the same as a full month weather forecast. Weather is only meaningful over the forecast horizon the provider supports; the remaining dates can still show your appointments.

For your particular requirement, I would test Readdle and Fantastical side by side, looking specifically at how much weather information remains visible when the entire month is on screen.
